items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose there is an exponential relationship of the form [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x] between the variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] shown in the semi-log scatter plot below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f98a3751586612016aa8f6b627f5144c]

Content:
Suppose further that the semi-log scatter plot has the trend line

Content:
[MATH: Y = 4 + 0.3x,]

Content:
where [MATH: Y = \log y.] Using only this information, it's possible to figure out the values of [MATH: a] and [MATH: b] in the exponential relationship [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x.]

Content:
The first step is to transform the exponential relationship into a linear form. We can do this by taking the logarithm of both sides of the equation:

Content:
[MATH: y|= a ⋅ b^{x}; \log y|= \log (a ⋅ b^{x}); \log y|= \log a + \log b^{x}; \log y|= \log a + x ⋅ \log b; Y|= A + Bx,]
where
[MATH: Y=\log y,\qquad
A=\log a,\qquad
B=\log b.]

Content:
Now, comparing [MATH: Y = A + Bx] with the equation [MATH: Y = 4 + 0.3x,] we obtain
[MATH: A = 4, \qquad B = 0.3.]

Content:
Finally, all that's left is to substitute the values above in the equations relating [MATH: A] to [MATH: a] and [MATH: B] to [MATH: b.]

Content:
- Substituting [MATH: A=4] into the equation relating [MATH: A] to [MATH: a,] we get
[MATH: \log a|= A; \log a|= 4; a|= 10^{4}; a|= 10000.]
- Substituting [MATH: B=0.3] into the equation relating [MATH: B] to [MATH: b,] we get
[MATH: \log b|= B; \log b|= 0.3; b|= 10^{0.3}; b|≈ 2.00,]
rounded to two decimal places.

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that the approximate relationship between [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] is given by

Content:
[MATH: y\approx 10\,000 \cdot 2^x.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Applying [MATH: \log] to both sides of [MATH: y = a \cdot b^x,] we get [MATH: y|= a ⋅ b^{x}; \log y|= \log (a ⋅ b^{x}); \log y|= \log a + \log b^{x}; \log y|= \log a + x ⋅ \log b; Y|= A + Bx,] where [MATH: Y=\log y,\qquad A=\log a,\qquad B=\log b.]

Comparing [MATH: Y = A + Bx] with the given equation [MATH: Y = 3 - 0.2x,] we obtain [MATH: A = 3, \qquad B = -0.2.]

As a result, we get [MATH: A|= 3; \log a|= 3; a|= 10^{3}; a|= 1000.]

Also,

[MATH: B|= − 0.2; \log b|= − 0.2; b|= 10^{− 0.2}; ≈ 0.63.]

items.title: Calculating Parameters by Finding the Slope or Y-Intercept of a Semi-Log Scatter Plot

sections.normalized_html:
There is an exponential relationship of the form [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x] between variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y.] The corresponding semi-log scatter plot with the associated trendline is shown above. Find the values of [MATH: a] and [MATH: b.] Round your answer to [MATH: 2] decimal places where appropriate.

Hint: The trend line passes close to the points [MATH: (3,4)] and [MATH: (9,6).]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/fa386c7595288c88852186bcc4b625fb]

There is an exponential relationship of the form [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x] between variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y.] The corresponding semi-log scatter plot with the associated trendline is shown above. Find the values of [MATH: a] and [MATH: b.] Round your answer to [MATH: 2] decimal places where appropriate.

Hint: The trend line passes close to the points [MATH: (3,4)] and [MATH: (9,6).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To get the corresponding semi-log plot, we apply [MATH: \log] to both sides of [MATH: y = a \cdot b^x.] This gives

[MATH: y|= a ⋅ b^{x}; \log y|= \log (a ⋅ b^{x}); \log y|= \log a + \log b^{x}; \log y|= \log a + x ⋅ \log b; Y|= A + Bx,]

where [MATH: Y=\log y , \qquad A=\log a, \qquad B=\log b.]

Let's now consider an approximate trend line [MATH: Y = A + Bx] for our data:

We now proceed to calculate the constants [MATH: a] and [MATH: b\mathbin{:}]

  • Looking at the trendline, the [MATH: Y]-intercept is [MATH: Y \approx 3.] Therefore, [MATH: A|≈ 3; \log_{10} a|≈ 3; a|≈ 10^{3}; a|= 1000.]

  • The trendline passes close to the points [MATH: (3,4)] and [MATH: (9,6).] Therefore, the line's slope is [MATH: B \approx \dfrac{6 - 4}{9 - 3} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}] and we obtain [MATH: B|≈ (1)/(3); \log b|≈ (1)/(3); b|≈ 10^{1/3}; = root(10, 3); ≈ 2.15] rounded to [MATH: 2] decimal places.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose there is an exponential relationship of the form [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x] between the variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] shown in the semi-log scatter plot below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f98a3751586612016aa8f6b627f5144c]

Content:
Suppose further that the semi-log scatter plot has the trend line

Content:
[MATH: Y = 4 + 0.3x,]

Content:
where [MATH: Y = \log y.] Using only this information, it's possible to figure out the values of [MATH: a] and [MATH: b] in the exponential relationship [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x.]

Content:
The first step is to transform the exponential relationship into a linear form. We can do this by taking the logarithm of both sides of the equation:

Content:
[MATH: y|= a ⋅ b^{x}; \log y|= \log (a ⋅ b^{x}); \log y|= \log a + \log b^{x}; \log y|= \log a + x ⋅ \log b; Y|= A + Bx,]
where
[MATH: Y=\log y,\qquad
A=\log a,\qquad
B=\log b.]

Content:
Now, comparing [MATH: Y = A + Bx] with the equation [MATH: Y = 4 + 0.3x,] we obtain
[MATH: A = 4, \qquad B = 0.3.]

Content:
Finally, all that's left is to substitute the values above in the equations relating [MATH: A] to [MATH: a] and [MATH: B] to [MATH: b.]

Content:
- Substituting [MATH: A=4] into the equation relating [MATH: A] to [MATH: a,] we get
[MATH: \log a|= A; \log a|= 4; a|= 10^{4}; a|= 10000.]
- Substituting [MATH: B=0.3] into the equation relating [MATH: B] to [MATH: b,] we get
[MATH: \log b|= B; \log b|= 0.3; b|= 10^{0.3}; b|≈ 2.00,]
rounded to two decimal places.

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that the approximate relationship between [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] is given by

Content:
[MATH: y\approx 10\,000 \cdot 2^x.]

---

Item 2 — Example: Calculating Exponential Parameters from Semi-Log Scatter Plots and Trend Line Equations

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/99e25b92d4b305584ced795c1c73d787]

There is an exponential relationship of the form [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x] between the variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y.] The corresponding semi-log scatter plot with the trend line [MATH: Y = 3 - 0.2x] is shown above. Estimate the values of [MATH: a] and [MATH: b.] Round your answers to [MATH: 2] decimal places where appropriate.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Applying [MATH: \log] to both sides of [MATH: y = a \cdot b^x,] we get
[MATH: y|= a ⋅ b^{x}; \log y|= \log (a ⋅ b^{x}); \log y|= \log a + \log b^{x}; \log y|= \log a + x ⋅ \log b; Y|= A + Bx,]
where
[MATH: Y=\log y,\qquad
A=\log a,\qquad
B=\log b.]

Comparing [MATH: Y = A + Bx] with the given equation [MATH: Y = 3 - 0.2x,] we obtain
[MATH: A = 3, \qquad B = -0.2.]

As a result, we get
[MATH: A|= 3; \log a|= 3; a|= 10^{3}; a|= 1000.]

Also,

[MATH: B|= − 0.2; \log b|= − 0.2; b|= 10^{− 0.2}; ≈ 0.63.]

Item 5 — Example: Calculating Parameters by Finding the Slope or Y-Intercept of a Semi-Log Scatter Plot

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/fa386c7595288c88852186bcc4b625fb]

There is an exponential relationship of the form [MATH: y \approx a \cdot b^x] between variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y.] The corresponding semi-log scatter plot with the associated trendline is shown above. Find the values of [MATH: a] and [MATH: b.] Round your answer to [MATH: 2] decimal places where appropriate.

Hint: The trend line passes close to the points [MATH: (3,4)] and [MATH: (9,6).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To get the corresponding semi-log plot, we apply [MATH: \log] to both sides of [MATH: y = a \cdot b^x.] This gives

[MATH: y|= a ⋅ b^{x}; \log y|= \log (a ⋅ b^{x}); \log y|= \log a + \log b^{x}; \log y|= \log a + x ⋅ \log b; Y|= A + Bx,]

where
[MATH: Y=\log y , \qquad A=\log a, \qquad B=\log b.]

Let's now consider an approximate trend line [MATH: Y = A + Bx] for our data:

[IMG: /graphics/32312fbdc16c10efeea613b7ef2f8f26]

We now proceed to calculate the constants [MATH: a] and [MATH: b\mathbin{:}]

- Looking at the trendline, the [MATH: Y]-intercept is [MATH: Y \approx 3.] Therefore,
[MATH: A|≈ 3; \log_{10} a|≈ 3; a|≈ 10^{3}; a|= 1000.]
- The trendline passes close to the points [MATH: (3,4)] and [MATH: (9,6).] Therefore, the line's slope is
[MATH: B \approx \dfrac{6 - 4}{9 - 3} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}]
and we obtain
[MATH: B|≈ (1)/(3); \log b|≈ (1)/(3); b|≈ 10^{1/3}; = root(10, 3); ≈ 2.15]
rounded to [MATH: 2] decimal places.
